priorities.name: Quiet space for focused work
priorities.issue: Common areas get noisy enough to interrupt concentrated work, and cold temperatures compound the difficulty of focusing.
whatItLooksLike: Again, the common areas are sometimes noisy and distracting.
It gets extremely cold sometimes and is hard to concentrate

evidence.text: Focused / Private Work is the #1 priority category (86/100).
Noise & Distraction: 17 people (17% of respondents), 24 comments, 75% negative; focused-work friction 28/100 (56% under-supported).

priorities.proposedAction: Review quiet-zone availability and etiquette in common areas before any physical change; test a designated quiet neighborhood.
priorities.siteMustDo: Observe common areas at peak, identify the noisiest zones, and pilot a quiet-zone protocol; track whether it helps.

priorities.name: Thermal comfort (temperature)
priorities.issue: Temperature — running cold — is a sharply negative, specific complaint that also undermines focus.
whatItLooksLike: It gets extremely cold sometimes and is hard to concentrate

evidence.text: Temperature / Thermal: 12 people (12% of respondents), 15 comments, 80% negative — the most-negative theme at the site.

priorities.proposedAction: Have facilities check HVAC set-points and balancing in the affected zones and confirm whether it's a control, zoning, or equipment issue.
priorities.siteMustDo: Log the specific cold zones and times, submit to building operations, and verify a fix rather than assuming set-point changes hold.

priorities.name: Network connectivity reliability
priorities.issue: Unreliable connectivity directly disrupts virtual work, and it registers above the company norm here.
whatItLooksLike: The internet connectivity is unreliable which directly affects all work. There are also no real food options on site so even basic logistics like lunch become a problem.

evidence.text: Connectivity is raised by 12% of respondents vs 14% company-wide.
Connectivity issues undercut an otherwise well-rated site (Index 72 ± 4, in line with the company average).

priorities.proposedAction: Validate Wi-Fi coverage/quality in the reported areas and route confirmed gaps to the Technology workstream.
priorities.siteMustDo: Collect the specific floors/areas and times of drops, run a coverage check, and escalate with data to Technology.

priorities.name: Private space for confidential calls and conversations
priorities.issue: Associates and people leaders with back-to-back virtual meetings on sensitive topics struggle to get private space, and on the open floor call participants can hear the background.
whatItLooksLike: …I have back to back online meetings, private office space for these meetings is severely incumbered when having to book office space.
…it can be challenging to fully participate when much of my work involves sensitive and confidential information. …
…No privacy I've been on calls with colleagues or clients hear background noise. …

evidence.text: Availability of spaces that support discretion: Under Supported — friction 19/100 (43% under-supported).
Tasks requiring discretion: Under Supported — friction 19/100 (37% under-supported).
Privacy & Confidentiality: 11 people (11% of respondents), 14 comments, 43% negative — the survey signal is stronger than the comment signal.
Distinct from P1: P1 is quiet for focused work; this is confidentiality for conversations.

priorities.proposedAction: Check how enclosed offices and rooms are booked on peak days, and hold a small set for short, walk-up confidential calls before considering any new enclosed space.
priorities.siteMustDo: Track when associates can't get a private room for a confidential call over two weeks, pilot the walk-up hold, and escalate a sized gap only if the pilot doesn't close it.

priorities.name: Dual monitors in offices, focus rooms and single-screen desks
priorities.issue: Several offices and focus rooms — and some desks — have a single monitor, so the enclosed rooms people need for calls are also the least productive places to work.
whatItLooksLike: I think all workstations should have dual monitors, not sure why we have some with only one,
Lack of quality chairs and dual monitors in the individual work rooms
…There is only one monitor in the offices which severely limit my ability to work efficiently. …

evidence.text: Hardware (Monitors / Peripherals): 16 people (16% of respondents), 24 comments, 62% negative; raised by 16% of respondents vs 22% company-wide.
Workplace-provided hardware agreement: 4.04 vs 3.80 company average (Strong).
Strong hardware agreement alongside specific single-monitor complaints points to a targeted gap in enclosed rooms, not a site-wide hardware problem.

priorities.proposedAction: Inventory monitors in every office and focus room and add a second monitor (with a compatible dock or cable) wherever the desk surface supports it.
priorities.siteMustDo: Complete the room-by-room monitor count, send Technology the list of single-monitor rooms and desks, and confirm the installs.
